analysis:
The supplied units are base_text excerpts (lines 610-1755) of the SSD prefix cache test file. The only PR change is a comment edit around base line 4361, which is outside the supplied excerpts. The patch is comment-only: it clarifies that SSDWriteBehind.consume charges the byte bucket per entry in array order when the whole donation does not fit. It alters no executable code, so no production logic, gate, TTL, key derivation, or AAD behavior changes.

I read the supplied test content against T-041. It exercises the security properties the threat model relies on: the DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE kill switch and test-root isolation, TTL capped at 1800s (env can only shorten), the disk budget resolver, HMAC-tagged filenames with no raw chain hashes, salt/scope isolation, corruption fallback that deletes and drops the index entry, symlink-safe reconciliation and removal, epoch stability across eviction/TTL/corrupt removal, and write-cap behavior. None of this is modified, so there is no regression or new attack surface. The tests are consistent with the T-041 documented posture, including the 30-minute TTL and epoch non-rotation on per-file removal.

The comment change documents existing write-cap ordering behavior, which affects only endurance/availability accounting. I verified no threat-model assumption is invalidated. Remaining limits: the hunk at ~4361 and the production SSDWriteBehind source were not supplied, so the comment's accuracy against the implementation is unverified. This has no security impact.
